meta.status: collection only; nothing in this file is on the map or in data/
meta.access_note: Pages were read with a page-reader tool, because the working container cannot reach these hosts directly. Most reads returned the page text; some returned the reader's own extract of the page instead (claims from those carry access = page_read_via_reader_extract). Each claim's evidence_text was checked by script against what the reader returned for that URL.
meta.stopped_agents_note: Some searches and reads in this batch were stopped by the account usage limit before they reported. Their searches and page-reader calls are logged in raw/ as returned, but produced no claims. Agents that were run again after the limit reset are listed in stats.agents_rerun_after_usage_limit; any still missing are in stats.agents_stopped_at_usage_limit.

evidence_check_values.normalized: found after normalising spaces, quote marks and dashes
evidence_check_values.normalized_ci: found after normalising and ignoring case
evidence_check_values.segments: excerpt contains an ellipsis; every part was found
evidence_check_values.not_found: not found in the captured page text: treat the claim as unverified
evidence_check_values.no_raw: no page text was captured for this URL
evidence_check_values.*_in_reader_extract: the page reader returned an extract rather than the page text; the excerpt was found in that extract (a page-text re-check is pending)
evidence_check_values.found_in_reader_extract_only: the page text was captured later and the excerpt is not in it word for word; it is only in the page reader's own extract, so treat the wording as unverified

meta.labels: fact | alleged | speculation | unproven_conspiracy | no_link. fact = the source states it (or the organisation published it about itself). label_scope says what the label covers.

map_status_values.pair_already_linked: both entities are on the map and already linked (see existing_relations)
map_status_values.new_tie_between_known_entities: both entities are on the map but not linked
map_status_values.new_entity_or_unmatched_name: one side matched a map entity, the other did not (new entity, or a name the matcher missed)
map_status_values.both_names_unmatched: neither side matched a map entity

pages.page_title: Iver Ørstavik honored with the Badge of Honor for Merits to the Administration of Justice - Ministry of Justice - Gov.pl website
pages.capture_answer: Ministry of Justice news item dated 12.06.2024. The ceremony took place at the Ministry of Justice. Minister of Justice Adam Bodnar gave Iver Ørstavik the Badge of Honor for Merits to the Administration of Justice (body text also calls it the Badge of Honor for Merits in the Field of Justice). Stated reasons: contributions to strengthening democratic-state principles, legal culture and the justice system. Bodnar cited Ørstavik's work on Norwegian-Polish NGO collaboration for the rule of law. Attendees: Deputy Minister of Justice Zuzanna Rudzińska-Bluszcz, Norwegian Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Marta Varteressian, Norwegian Ambassador to Poland Øystein Bø, and unnamed Polish NGO and academic representatives. Ørstavik is called an activist with the Rafto Foundation for Human Rights, not a Rafto adviser. The page does not mention a Norway Grants freeze, Ziobro, support for Polish judges, or any amount. No funders, organiser details or party affiliations are stated.

pages.capture_answer: Norwegian government page dated 12/06/2024 with the text of State Secretary Maria Varteressian's remarks at the Badge of Honour ceremony for Iver Ørstavik. Remarks: Ørstavik is a 'human rights advisor' who has worked with Rafto laureates and, per the speaker, with Polish rule-of-law and civil-society figures including Bodnar (2018 Rafto Prize laureate). The page has no statement on the 2020 freeze, the 2026 Justice programme, resumed justice cooperation, or any amount. Varteressian's party is not stated. The page does not call Ørstavik a Rafto Foundation adviser. Her title and first name differ from the Polish page (Deputy Minister, 'Marta').

pages.capture_answer: The landing page has only the title and a link to the PDF. The PDF is the exhibit set (Exhibits 1 to 5, 21 pages) from Case 1:12-cv-02034-RBW, Document 31-1, filed 09/16/15. Its docket notices come from Judicial Watch, Inc. v. Department of State, No. 1:13-cv-01363-EGS (D.D.C.), a FOIA suit about former Secretary Clinton's private email server and State Department records. The exhibits are minute orders dated July 31, August 7 and August 20, 2015; a September 2, 2015 letter from the State Department to the FBI General Counsel; State Department letters to the FBI Director and to Clinton's attorney; a June 15, 2015 reply from that attorney; and a NARA letter dated July 2, 2016 (OCR 'JUL. 0 2 2016'). The FOIA request they describe seeks Huma Abedin's SF-50 personnel forms, State Department contracts with her, and records of her outside employment. No released record names Free Courts, Batory, HFHR, Iustitia, Themis or DemoCrisis, or shows State or embassy money to any of them. No amounts appear. The exhibits do not mention Poland, a US embassy, or the Open Society Foundations. Officials' names are in names_listed.

pages.capture_answer: The programme 'Strengthening Democratic Resilience and Civil Society in Poland' is listed for Action For Democracy. Legal form and location come from the linked funder profile: '501(c)(4) organization', Chicago, IL, EIN 87-4640498. The page gives only the name 'Action For Democracy', with no separate legal name. The country 'United States' is inferred, not written. Programme amount: 'Not stated' on the listing; the profile shows 'Amount Varies'. The $318K figure is the funder's total 2024 grants (one grant, $317,960 in the profile table, to Khmer Democratic Rescue Foundation, Pomona, CA), not this programme's budget. Dates: rolling (quarterly review); 'Tracked since April 2026'; the listing also gives a first-round deadline of 'July 17, 6pm CET (2023)'. Eligibility: non-governmental, non-partisan CSOs based in Poland, with national reach or rural operation valued, and compliant with all Polish and U.S. rules, including electoral and campaign finance laws. Named grantees for Poland: none. Places where the profile says the funder has awarded grants: California, District of Columbia, New York, Virginia. Iustitia, Themis, Free Courts / Wolne Sądy, HFHR, Batory Foundation, KOS, OKO.press, Akcja Demokracja and KOD are not named. Funder board (2024 filing, per profile): David Koranyi (Board President; compensation $298K in 2024), Christopher Maroshegyi (Board Treasurer; $27K), Elisabeth Jennings (Board Secretary), Roberto Patino (Board Member). The funder's own grantee list was not checked: its website is linked from the profile but sits on another host. The 2022 and 2023 grantee names did not come through in the fetched text. No TK judge, Tusk, Wawrykiewicz, Żurek, Święczkowski or Nawrocki appears.

pages.capture_answer: Batory's CERV-funded Equal Rights Programme, thematic round (Decision 1856, 5 Nov 2025): 40 large grants (PLN 4,958,807) and 40 small grants (PLN 2,514,278). Free Courts (PLN 121,293 requested), HFHR (124,976), Akcja Demokracja (124,904), ISP (124,874) and the Kultura Liberalna Foundation (125,000) applied and were not granted, and no reserve lists were created. Iustitia, Themis, OKO.press, KOD, the Osiatyński Archive, Moje Państwo, the Hołda Association and INPRIS are not among the 80 granted. Committee chair: Joanna Pietruszka.

pages.fetch_note: Complaint, Judicial Watch, Inc. v. U.S. Department of State, U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, No. 1:26-cv-00346. Dated 4 Feb 2026; the court stamp shows 5 Feb 2026. Counsel: James F. Peterson. It has one FOIA count. The FOIA request of 12 Nov 2025 (ref. F-2026-02738) covers 1 Jan 2016 to the present. Items A-D seek State Department contracts and grant agreements with Free Courts ('Wolne Sady'), Civil Liberties Union for Europe, DemoCrisis and Ökotárs Alapítvány (Hungary). Item E seeks all State emails and cables mentioning these four groups. The complaint says no determination was made and no records were produced. It names no grant or amount and does not mention NED, OSF, Batory, HFHR, Iustitia or OKO.press. It references no exhibits.

pages.page_title: Umowy zawarte w 2024 roku
pages.capture_answer: The MoJ register for 2024 (visible rows January to mid-June 2024, Bodnar's term as minister) lists paid opinion contracts. Patyra: PLN 3,000 (5 Jan, prosecution law). Rakowska's law office: PLN 3,001.20 and Kuca: PLN 3,000 (5 Jan, art. 47 of the 2016 introductory act to the Prosecution Law). Zalasiński, Urbaniak and Zaleśny: PLN 4,000 each (17-24 Jan, scope of TK interim measures). Kmieciak: two rows of PLN 3,723 (26 Feb, effects of the TK interim orders of 1 Feb 2024). Piotrowski: PLN 4,000 (4 Mar, effects of TK interim orders). Future TK judge Dziurda: PLN 8,000 (2-22 Apr, analysis of the draft law transposing the EU representative-actions directive). Other rows cover seconding judges to the MoJ, cancelling judicial competitions, presidential consent to deputy prosecutor appointments, lay judges (Gwizdak, PLN 20,333.23) and an audit firm's Justice Fund analysis (PLN 142,950.60). The visible rows contain no contract with the other six Sejm-elected TK judges, nor with Batory, HFHR, Iustitia, Themis or Free Courts.
